svg.text: ESP32-CAM camera · Raspberry Pi client · laptop server · SerBot robot
Serial is crossed: Pi TXD → ESP U0R, ESP U0T → Pi RXD. IO0 wire only matters when flashing.
One shared Wi-Fi network (2.4 GHz): video and results both travel over it
5 V regulated → Pi USB-C power in (Pi 5: 5 A · Pi 4: 3 A) + common GND
Powers the camera board. Use 5 V, not 3V3: Wi-Fi current peaks brown out the 3.3 V pin.
Common ground. Serial does not work without it.
Pi → ESP serial: flash firmware, send commands.
ESP → Pi serial: boot log and the camera's IP address.
Drive LOW, then press RST = flash mode. Otherwise keep it an input: IO0 is also the camera clock.
Regulated 5 V from the robot battery. Check SerBot's output rating first.
Spoken prompts (client.py --speak). The Pi 5 has no jack, so use a USB speaker there.
• Both boards use 3.3 V logic, so the serial wires connect directly with no level shifter.
• Enable the Pi UART: sudo raspi-config → Interface Options → Serial Port → login shell No, hardware Yes. It appears as /dev/serial0.
• All video goes over the shared Wi-Fi; the wires carry only power and serial. Flash the CameraWebServer sketch (AI-Thinker), then on the Pi:
• ESP32 radios are 2.4 GHz only, so the ESP32-CAM, Pi and laptop must all join the 2.4 GHz network (not a 5 GHz-only SSID).
• Each frame crosses the same Wi-Fi twice (ESP32 → Pi, then Pi → laptop). If it lags, set the ESP32 to VGA 640×480 or lower client.py --quality.
• GPIO7 is pulled high while the Pi boots, so the ESP32-CAM starts normally when both power on together.
• SerBot's control link is not in the code yet: the robot is simulated (robot/simulated.py) until a BaseRobot driver exists.
